interpretation.interpretation: The diagram appears to represent the geocentric cosmos as seven concentric planetary orbits around a central Earth. The central dot would be the Earth, and each of the seven concentric circles would be the orbit of one of the seven planets (Moon, Mercury, Venus, Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn). The heads placed on a vertical axis at the top of each circle would be personifications of the planets. The orange head with radiating lines in the fourth circle from the outside would be the Sun, which sits in the middle of the series of seven. The head with a crescent-like mark on the second circle from the centre would be the Moon, or possibly a nearby planet. The outermost circle would be Saturn and the innermost circle the Moon, following the usual order of the planets in the Ptolemaic scheme. The text on the page around the diagram probably explains the order and distances of the planetary spheres, but no label is part of the diagram itself.
interpretation.evidence: The diagram has seven concentric circles around a central dot, with seven heads aligned on one vertical axis, one per circle. This matches medieval diagrams of the planetary spheres. The only head that stands out is the orange, radiating one in the fourth position, which fits the Sun in the middle of the sequence. This also fits the order of the planets in the geocentric system. There is no transcribed label inside the diagram, so the identification of the individual planets rests on visual features and diagrammatic tradition, not on text. Step 1 did not record the marginal text of the page, which is not part of the diagram. In Step 1, the heads were related to the circles with 'connected_to' on the basis of overlap, which is a weak reading. The identification of the second head from the centre as the Moon is uncertain, since the crescent-shaped mark is small and unclear.
